slides.title: If someone watched how you carry yourself, what would they learn?

body.text: This is fighting for touches or an underhook.

items: Whoever gets there first wins, whether by three touches or by the underhook plus closed hands.

body.text: This is catching an arm and locking hands.

items: The bottom player wins by locking his hands with an underhook after a post.
The top player wins by standing and opening the guard.

body.text: This is staying on someone's back.

items: The top player holds as long as he keeps chest-to-back contact.
The bottom player wins by getting his back flat to the mat, or by facing and coming on top.

slides.title: What made it work?
slides.question: Tonight you held full control standing, passing, and on his back, without ever reaching for the finish. What did that teach whoever was watching?

options.text: That control, not the finish, is the lesson.
options.feedback: Control without reaching for the finish teaches more than any finish could.

options.text: That finishing fast is what matters most.
options.feedback: Finishing fast is not the lesson a newer partner actually needs.

options.text: Nothing, since you never finished anything.
options.feedback: Not finishing on purpose is still teaching something.
